answer:
**Softmax contrastive learning asks which candidate is the match; sigmoid learning asks whether each pair matches.** In CLIP's batch objective, the correct text competes against other texts in a shared normalization. Increasing one candidate's probability changes the normalized probabilities of the others. SigLIP applies a binary match/non-match loss to each evaluated pair. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15343)

For an image with one matched caption and many mismatched captions, sigmoid training pushes the matched pair's score upward and mismatched scores downward independently through their binary losses. A learned scale and bias help set the score range and decision baseline. The absence of a global softmax denominator makes the pairwise computation easier to partition in some implementations.

**Independent losses do not eliminate negative-pair cost.** A batch of b images and b texts still has $b^2$ possible pairs. Computing all of them requires work, while sampling a subset changes coverage and weighting. With many more negatives than positives, loss normalization and bias are important parts of the method.

Compare the objectives under matched data, compute, and evaluation. Reported batch-size advantages are empirical findings for particular training setups, not a theorem that sigmoid always converges better. Distributed performance also depends on where embeddings and pair blocks are placed. The useful distinction is the training comparison being made, not simply whether the formula contains a softmax or a sigmoid.

**Technical details and references.**

CLIP normalizes each image/text score against batch alternatives with softmax. SigLIP trains matched and mismatched pairs using independent sigmoid binary losses, with a learned scale/bias convention. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.15343)

$$L=-\sum_{ij}\log\sigma(y_{ij}(s_{ij}+b)),\qquad y_{ij}\in\{-1,+1\}.$$

Pairwise losses avoid requiring a global softmax denominator and allow flexible distribution of pair computations. Negative-pair count, sampling, and weighting still matter; sigmoid does not make the full all-pairs cost disappear. Reported advantages at particular batch sizes are empirical, not a guarantee of stability for every configuration. Compare matched compute, data, negative coverage, and downstream retrieval/classification; distributed communication depends on how embeddings and pair blocks are exchanged.
